blocks.heading: What today is
blocks.body: About 100 minutes. Do the lab in the app. The check at the end uses words from today only.

blocks.heading: The week’s apple
blocks.body:
Three pages. Three jobs. One folder.

You still do **not** make a booklet. A booklet is a table of contents that points at files. That is week 3. Stay in the folder. Do not hunt for extra views.

blocks.heading: INDEX.txt
blocks.body: A three-line list in a text file. That is your memory, not the published book.

blocks.title: Getting Started with DITA Using Oxygen XML Editor
watchFor: Three topic types in one project

blocks.heading: Do the work
blocks.body:
This lab can fail. Fail when: A file is missing, a file is the wrong type, or a red error remains.

Expected: Three clean files and a three-line INDEX.txt.

blocks.intro: Walk the steps in order. Tick them in the lab after you actually do them.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.body: Put these three files in oxygen-bootcamp-work/week2/ (copy from flower-docs if you drifted): what-a-cut-flower.dita, change-the-water.dita, studio-hours.dita.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.body: Open each one. No red error. Each still matches its type: explaining, how-to, lookup.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.body: Write a three-line index in oxygen-bootcamp-work/week2/INDEX.txt: file name :  kind of page :  one-line summary.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.body: Do not build a table of contents in Oxygen yet. The text index is enough. The booklet is week 3.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.body: If a page is the wrong type, make a new file from the right template and move the words. Do not pretend.

blocks.summary: Three clean files and a three-line INDEX.txt.

blocks.q: Why three files instead of one long page?
options: Because later you can mix and reuse them in a booklet
Because Oxygen cannot open long files
blocks.why: Small pages are easier to fix and, next week, easier to list in a table of contents.

options: A simple list so you know what you have before week 3
blocks.why: Next week you will make a real table of contents in Oxygen. Today, a text list is the apple.
